notesStmt.note: A note on the verso, in Whitman's hand, indicates that this was intended to be sent to the printer Henry Curtz, who often set up Whitman's poems in type so that the poet could see how they looked on the printed page. The manuscript also contains markings in Whitman's hand, concerning the formatting of the text, clearly intended for the printer. This suggests that the manuscript was composed not long before the poem's publication, likely in early 1891.

This manuscript, composed of three scraps pasted together, is a draft of "Old Chants," which was first published in Truth on March 19, 1891. The poem was then reprinted in Good-Bye My Fancy (1891). The note at the bottom of the recto is in the hand of Horace Traubel.

body.head: Old Chants.

lg.l: An ancient song reciting, ending,
Once, gazing toward thee, Mother of All,
Musing, seeking themes fitted for thee,
Accept for me, thou saidst, the elder ballads,

l.hi:
And name for me before thou goest each ancient
poet.

lg.l: (Of ‸many debts incalculable,

Haply the our New World's chiefest debt is to the
old poems.)
Ever so far back, preluding thee, America,
First Old Chants, Egyptian priests and those of Ethiopia,
The Hindu epics, the Grecian, Chinese, Persian,

The Biblic books and prophets, the deeps idylls of
the Nazarene,

The Iliad, Odyssey, plots, doings, wanderings
of Eneas,
Hesiod, Eschylus, Sophocles, Merlin, Arthur,
The Cid, Roland at Roncesvalles, the Nibelungen,
The troubadours, minstrels, minnesingers, skalds,
Chaucer, Dante, flocks of singing birds,

The Border Minstrelsy, the bye-gone ballads, feudal
tales, essays, plays,
Shakspere, Schiller, Walter Scott, Tennyson,
As some vast wondrous ‸wierdweird dream⹀presences,
Some great shadowy group gathering around

Darting their mighty masterful eyes forward
at thee,

Thou! with as now thy bending neck and
head, with courteous hand and word, ‸ascending,

Thou! pausing a moment, drooping thine
eyes upon them, as blent with their music,

l.add: Well pleased, accepting all, curiously prepared for,

lg.l: Thou enterest at thy entrance porch.
